title: North Greenbush Flock vendor request reconciliation
summary: Request #1897 resolves Flock Safety as the independently reported current ALPR vendor in North Greenbush by March 2026, while leaving contracts, exact equipment, ownership, administration, and sharing details unresolved pending primary records.

sources.title: Town of North Greenbush Police Department
Residents question proposal for automatic license plate reader at Poestenkill intersection
Calls mount to remove Flock Safety cameras in Troy

data.question: Can the current/historical ALPR vendor for North Greenbush be resolved from public evidence, and what deployment details remain unsupported?
data.method: Reconciled the existing canonical North Greenbush vendor target against November 2025 and March 2026 Times Union reporting plus current first-party town and police web surfaces.
data.framework: Vendor identification, installation, ownership, procurement, administration, sharing, and actual use remain separate evidence states. Secondary reporting can resolve the vendor lead without establishing contract or configuration details.
data.scope: Public organizational and municipal ALPR evidence for North Greenbush; no private-person enrichment.
findings: November 2025 reporting stated that local police had installed automatic plate readers in North Greenbush.
March 17, 2026 Times Union reporting specifically stated that Flock cameras were currently installed in North Greenbush.

The Town of North Greenbush and North Greenbush Police Department maintain current first-party public web surfaces, but no reviewed primary record in this pass established the Flock contract, camera count, locations, serials, activation dates, administrators, or sharing configuration.
conclusions: Flock Safety is now a defensible current vendor identification for the reported North Greenbush ALPR deployment at the level of independent local reporting.
The existing canonical target remains open because procurement, equipment, ownership, administration, audit, and sharing evidence is incomplete.
recommendations: Recover contracts, quotes, grants, purchase orders, renewals, and exact camera inventory.
Recover Organization Audit, Network Audit, users/admins, event logs, and directed sharing edges.
counterarguments: The local reporting may compress ownership or operational control, so exact town/police/vendor responsibility still requires primary records.
limitations: No native Flock contract or export was recovered.
No exact camera count, location inventory, serial, or activation date was established.
unresolved: What procurement instrument established the North Greenbush deployment?
Who owns, administers, maintains, and can query it?
What inbound and outbound sharing edges exist?
